title: On Intelligence and Its Specifications
description: A lay-readable book on the mathematics of optimal intelligence and what it implies about modern AI. It develops the clean theory of optimal prediction and decision (Bayesian inference, Solomonoff induction, and expected-utility maximization, synthesized as AIXI), then turns to the bounded systems that approximate it (large language models), and argues that the gap between the theory and the practice is where the specification problem, and AI safety, live. Seventeen chapters across four parts, written for the determined lay reader, with diagrams carrying much of the conceptual weight.
